question: Can tracked nonoverlapping private Metal heap backing for unchanged encoded records reduce load or idle query delay without larger scientific residency?

parameters.one_factor: Tracked placement-heap backing for unchanged immutable encoded record buffers; same kernel, 64-record submissions, mixed-tail options, source/read/authentication/staging and exact index.
parameters.defaults: Off, package-internal option only; app/public API unchanged.
parameters.planned_matrix: Fresh-process A1 standalone / B16 heap / A2 standalone, full66 load/index, frozen products, nine native replay masks, warm plus 4s idle, repeated cycles; retain every load and parity result.
parameters.memory: Freeze scientific bytes; explicitly admit and log Metal alignment and heap allocation bytes. No raw 4D duplicate or aliasing.
parameters.gate: Small nonoverlap/readback/budget/failure tests before all66. Any incorrect count, leaked allocation, loading regression or unreplicated wall improvement rejects promotion.
parameters.timing: Prepared archive/source pages unspecified. Not arbitrary-source cold HDF5 or native FPS.
parameters.preflight_result: 3/3 pass: exact disjoint readback, invalid plan rejection, real encoded hash failure/join/retry and allocation release. Initial Sendable warnings fixed with caller-serialized per-slot owned state; original log retained.
parameters.decision: NOT ADOPTED:135warm+54idle exact full66 comparisons and nine cross-arm full66 hashes pass. Warm timing neutral. Idle improvements mixed; case0 regresses and case5/6 do not beat both controls. Heap loads14.417/14.428s are slower than standalone14.119-14.211s, so no load nonregression acceptance.
